commands.review_summary:
The branch makes Discord tail errors, panics, and timeouts durably recoverable; adds fallback spooling and exact create/update/delete replay; bounds handler and repair shutdown; and adds replay-only CLI operation.

Reproducibility: yes. from source with high confidence: a handler can exceed its deadline while holding the single writable SQLite connection, preventing the outer failure recorder from durably identifying the exact message before tail exit. Focused tests exercise pool starvation, detached timeouts, shutdown races, and below-cursor replay, though no live Discord failure run is included.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] An area owner should decide whether to adopt the new fail-closed timeout and durable replay contract; there is no narrow mechanical defect for an automated repair lane.

target.title: fix: keep tail alive and replay timed-out messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A message handler can exceed its deadline while holding Discrawl's single writable SQLite connection. The outer failure recorder then cannot begin its own transaction, so the tail exits without a durable exact-message recovery identity. Delete failures also cannot be repaired by the existing fetch-and-upsert replay path.

The same shutdown boundary must prevent later ordered work and scheduled repair work from continuing across a replacement tail, while keeping diagnostics free of message content, payloads, panic values, tokens, and raw transport errors.

## What Changed

- Make `Client.Tail` the sole durable owner for every message-scoped returned error, panic, and timeout.
- Persist normalized create, update, or delete event identity in the failure ledger.
- Attempt bounded ledger persistence, then atomically spool a private content-free fallback when the writable connection is unavailable.
- Import fallback occurrences exactly once before Gateway startup and before maintenance replay candidate selection.
- Preserve repeated unresolved occurrences with per-occurrence receipts instead of discarding them.
- Bound and classify handler cancellation/join behavior; stop later ordered dequeue after a detached timeout.
- Cancel and join scheduled repair before client shutdown, with a fatal bounded timeout.
- Recover delete failures by marking canonical state deleted without an exact fetch, synthetic `message_events`, cursor changes, publishing, or `tail:last_event` movement.
- Delete FTS state through deterministic rowid-only SQL and retain embedding cleanup.
- Keep Gateway-open failures typed and separate from message-failure persistence.
- Emit only allowlisted stage, join, pool-wait, SQLite-code, ledger, and fallback timing fields.

## Evidence

Current head: `511dbe128010b0b9270e3b3bbf89d0f42027896f`

- `go test -count=1 ./...`
- `go test -count=1 -race ./...`
- Filtered repository coverage: `85.2%` against the `85.0%` floor
- `go vet ./...`
- `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`, `deadcode`, `gofumpt`, and `gosec`
- `go mod verify` and `go mod tidy -diff`
- Native build plus Linux and Windows cross-builds
- CLI metadata, status, TUI JSON, help, and version smoke checks
- Independent Pinchy repair review completed two passes and returned zero blockers

Focused tests cover one-owner create/update/delete recording, pool starvation fallback, external `SQLITE_BUSY`, concurrent fallback occurrences, atomic no-replace persistence, exactly-once imports across cleanup failures, path replacement resistance, event-aware replay, canonical delete recovery, rowid-constrained FTS deletion, bounded handler and repair joins, shutdown races, post-deadline nil handling, privacy-safe diagnostics, and Gateway-open classification.
